articles.title: SpaceX To Invest $74 Billion Into Data Center Construction Projects In Texas, Arizona
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from the Hill: Elon Musk's SpaceX plans to invest more than $74 billion into building two data centers in Texas and Arizona, the company announced Thursday, marketing them as projects that will boost local communities amid backlash surrounding such facilities. "These investments will expand local tax bases, generate substantial new revenue for schools and public services, and create economic opportunities that extend far beyond the facilities themselves," the company said in a release. SpaceX said it will put more than $24 billion into a new project in Texas's Rio Grande Valley, expanding the company's headquarters in Starbase -- a coastal town the tech giant established in 2025 in a previously unincorporated area of Cameron County. In Arizona, SpaceX will invest around $50 billion in Cochise County, a rural area east of Tucson bordering Mexico and New Mexico. SpaceX pledged the new projects will be created cooperatively with the surrounding communities and will be environmentally conscious. The company said the project in Texas would generate its own power and invest $220 million to expand the water supply in nearby Brownsville. While in Arizona, it vowed to work with local electric cooperatives and "potentially" reduce electric bills, saying the site would use dry cooling without water consumption. "They require strong partnerships with local communities, responsible environmental stewardship, and stable, competitive policies that give companies the confidence to make long-term investments," the company said in a release. Both sites promise hundreds of permanent jobs even once construction is complete. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: 'Speed is not a creative strategy': Adobe execs say that while AI is delivering results faster, its humans who still bring the quality
articles.content: If one thing's certain about AI, it's that it's made it easier than ever to produce professional-looking content – but it's just as easy to create poor-quality content, and Adobe itself will tell you that. That's why the company argues that, despite initial concerns about AI threatening the roles of creative professionals, human expertise is actually becoming more valuable. Speaking to the media in a fireside Q&A at its annual Adobe Max conference, company Product Marketing VP Deepa Subramaniam and Creative VP Resh Sidhu offered fresh perspectives on how judgment, ideas and creative direction are shining through. They argued that while AI can help users generate content at a much faster speed, it can't necessarily take the creative direction decision. While the company was keen to push trust and precision as two themes at this year's sessions, serving its tools as ideation platforms was also a clear emphasis. More quantity can actually be helpful to businesses looking to stand out "Speed is a capability, it's not a creative strategy," Sidhu affirmed, calling for humans to add elements of taste, craft and judgement. "You can create a thousand options of something – you still need someone to decide that's the thing that's worth making." The belief is largely that more non-designers can become designers – for example, writers will be able to visualize their concepts without having to learn specific apps or wait for colleagues to assist them. By throwing more perspectives into the pot, it also means companies can have access to more ideas and, according to Adobe, separate out more high-quality content from average content. Subramaniam also hinted at the traditionally steep learning curve associated with its flagship apps, noting that someone highly skilled in Photoshop might previously have struggled to produce motion graphics in After Effects without investing considerable learning time or enlisting a trained colleague. But even as the technical barriers associated with producing content continue to fall, the company believes expertise could become an even more important differentiator among creators. In short, while AI is undoubtedly shifting something, it's not the importance of human skills. We're in the midst of a transition where AI is both making specialist capabilities more accessible, but it's also highlighting the importance of human expertise and judgment. The VPs both summarized by agreeing that producing more content doesn't necessarily mean producing better work, positioning AI as an enabler but not a replacer.
articles.author: Craig Hale

articles.title: Hands-On With the New Apple TV 4K and Siri AI
articles.content: The 4th-generation Apple TV 4K with an A19 chip and Siri AI support is available starting on November 13, and we were able to spend some time with it ahead of launch. Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos. ‌Siri‌ AI is the headline feature, and while it's not perfect, it works better than the prior version of ‌Siri‌. ‌Siri‌ was able to pull up multiple movie and TV show recommendations and answer questions about content. Apple says ‌Siri‌ AI is in beta, and there's more work to be done. ‌Siri‌ AI wasn't great at answering follow-up questions, and only did so part of the time. There are far-field microphones in the set-top box, so you can just say "Hey ‌Siri‌" to activate ‌Siri‌ without having to use the remote. The ‌Apple TV‌ can recognize up to six people, so you can get personalized recommendations and context when talking to ‌Siri‌. The person who sets up the ‌Apple TV‌ needs to have an iPhone or iPad that supports ‌Siri‌ AI for ‌Siri‌ AI to work on the ‌Apple TV‌, and personal context also requires each user to have their own ‌Siri‌ AI-compatible device. The 2nd- and 3rd-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models will get ‌Siri‌ AI with the upcoming tvOS 27.2.1 update . Apple didn't change the design of the ‌Apple TV‌ 4K or update the look of the ‌Siri‌ Remote, but the remote does have new capabilities. It has a speaker built in so you can have it play a sound when it's lost, and Precision Finding is available if you have an iPhone Air , iPhone Duo , or iPhone 17 and later (excluding iPhone 17e ). The tvOS interface feels faster with the A19 chip, and it should be better for games if you play Apple Arcade titles on your TV. You can also pair four HomePod speakers to the ‌Apple TV‌ for surround sound, a feature that's unique to the latest model. Unfortunately, Apple is charging $299 for the 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K. It's twice as expensive as the prior-generation version was at this same time last year, and that's a wild increase. It's probably not worth upgrading if you already have a 2nd- or 3rd-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K, but if you have something older, it might be worth paying the money to get the new features. articles.title: GitHub availability report: October 2026
articles.content: We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability. The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery. As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity. That capacity is already carrying real growth. Migrated-service traffic has increased 82% since March, with Central US absorbing the growth beyond the highest weekly-average load previously served from our existing datacenter. This gives GitHub more room to grow without pushing the original environment beyond its prior operating range. We also made several targeted reliability improvements. Actions changes increased capacity for critical Azure control-plane requests. A separate NAT-gateway mitigation reduced usage by 85%; four production jobs failed during the change, compared with approximately 800 expected without the mitigation. Connection limits and other client improvements now also reduce the chance that a dependency interruption becomes a broader reconnect storm. We removed concentrated sources of database load as well. A high-traffic GitHub Actions endpoint handling more than 250 million requests per day moved to a more efficient service path, reducing peak database reads by 85%. Requiring at least three characters before searching repository topics reduced slow or terminated queries for that pattern by approximately 98%. Reliability was still not where it needed to be. The October 7 write outages exposed an unsafe interaction between database orchestration and production routing. An October 29 Azure network disruption affected all three Central US availability zones and at least 34,128 signed-in users. More details on these and other incidents follow. The East US 3 buildout is about one week behind plan. The next phase starts with its first validated traffic ramp in the first week of December, while we continue hardening migration safety, dependency isolation, and regional recovery. The principle remains the same: availability, then capacity, then features. October 05 19:11 UTC (lasting 3 hours and 38 minutes) Duration: approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes. Customers may have seen GitHub Actions jobs on GitHub-hosted runners stay queued much longer than usual, and some workflow runs failed to start. During the worst stretch, which lasted about 90 minutes, most jobs on GitHub-hosted runners did not start within five minutes. Impact eased as we failed over to healthy regions and added capacity. Self-hosted runners were not affected. GitHub Pages sites that build with actions were slow to update, though existing sites continued to serve normally. Some customers also saw errors in repository lists, licensing and billing pages, and some Copilot features. What went wrong and why? Actions jobs stayed queued or failed to start because the service that assigns jobs to GitHub-hosted runners stopped working reliably. A partial networking failure on our cloud provider’s side disrupted some of the connections between one of our datacenter regions and the cloud-hosted databases that service depends on. Instead of failing fast, the service waited for those calls to time out. The waiting calls piled up until the service ran out of memory and restarted. Jobs then shifted to the same service in a healthy region, which did not have enough capacity for the extra demand and began failing too. At the same time, runners that went several minutes without…

articles.title: Siri AI Coming to Older Apple TV 4K Models in tvOS 27.2.1
articles.content: An upcoming tvOS 27.2.1 update will bring Siri AI to the 2nd- and 3rd-generation Apple TV 4K models, according to Apple. A support document outlining ‌Siri‌ AI requirements across Apple products says tvOS 27.2.1 supports ‌Siri‌ AI on the ‌Apple TV‌ 4K (2nd generation and later), but the software hasn't yet been released. While older ‌Apple TV‌ models will need tvOS 27.2.1 for ‌Siri‌ AI, Apple appears to have a special ‌Siri‌ AI build of tvOS 27.2 for the 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K. Reviewers were able to test ‌Siri‌ AI on review units, and we can confirm it's working on our own review unit running tvOS 27.2. The 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K ships with tvOS 27.0, and users are prompted to update it to tvOS 27.2 during the setup process. Apple hasn't said when tvOS 27.2.1 will be released with ‌Siri‌ AI for older ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models, but it could come as soon as Friday. The latest ‌Apple TV‌ is priced at $299, and it features an A19 chip and an updated ‌Siri‌ Remote that has a Find My speaker and Precision Finding support. ‌Siri‌ AI on the ‌Apple TV‌ requires a nearby paired ‌Siri‌ AI-enabled device like an iPhone 15 Pro or later. articles.title: United Airlines becomes the latest enterprise to shut its door to customer bots
articles.content: United Airlines on Wednesday became the latest enterprise to block customer bots, following similar moves from Walmart, Target and Amazon. The $59 billion airline, the second largest in the world, said the move was prompted by fears of data leakage, unintended purchases, and the risk of violating federal airline rules. But industry observers say that the more concerning business risks are the lack of industry standardization around AI coupled with an ever-increasing number of bots from major AI vendors and AI startups. The fear is that supporting the multiple bots that customers use could become an almost infinite drain on IT resources. However, they said, strictly enforced industry standards might persuade some enterprises to rethink their bot resistance. United’s statement said, “United is taking steps to restrict access – directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators – to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants. This work includes updates to our booking, ticketing and distribution policies.” It pointed out that corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents, and said, “we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety.” The airline listed a variety of problems with bots that it is trying to avoid, including the risks associated with customers sharing account credentials “with personal, third-party, AI assistants [that] can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles.” It also spoke of regulatory challenges: “These automated AI actions have the potential to violate FAA [United States Federal Aviation Administration] and DOT [US Department of Transportation] regulations,” such as those stating that flight check-in requires human acknowledgment that bags do not contain banned substances like explosives. However, the airline sent a clear signal to the industry that it was willing to reconsider the ban if there are sufficient changes. “As personal AI assistants evolve, United will continue to evaluate how these tools interact with our services, with a focus on protecting our customers,” the statement said. Separating the humans from the bots One of the bigger enterprise concerns about agents is that, because they are using the customer’s credentials, the bot activity is typically indistinguishable from the human customer’s activity. Analysts say that the cleanest way to address that is to simply assign bots their own credentials. Last month, Walmart got close to that goal, putting in place a program, scheduled to start this month, to try to differentiate bot and human actions. “Today, when a customer uses an AI agent, it signs in using a customer’s account. This means that all purchases – whether made by the customer or the agent – appear together, without any differentiation,” its announcement said. “Agent Profiles, launching in the next month, will offer a new level of transparency for customers. Customers will be able to authorize each AI agent with a dedicated profile within the customer’s account, so the customers will be able to see the agent’s purchases separately from the rest of their purchases.” Target, on the other hand, blocked all but a handful of approved agents in recent changes to its terms and conditions , granting access only to Target’s AI Shopping Assistant, OAI, Google and Microsoft, although it said it may ”add, remove, or otherwise modify the list of Approved Agents at any time and in its sole discretion.” Any other agentic commerce tools, it said, “are unauthorized, expressly prohibited, and may not be used to access, log into, scrape, query, or otherwise interact with or gather data from the Site under any circumstances, whether directly or through API call(s), automated use of user credentials, or other…

articles.title: Nintendo Takes Down Switch Emulators, Mod Chip Firmware in Massive GitHub DMCA Sweep
articles.content: Nintendo has issued four DMCA takedown notices targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware such as Picofly, SX Core and HWFLY. As a result, 144 repositories containing firmware used to circumvent the console's copy protections have been removed by GitHub and replaced by a DMCA takedown notice. IGN reports: GitHub has posted Nintendo's November 6 DMCA notice, which says, "The Nintendo Switch console and video games contain technological protection measures ('TPMs') that permit the Nintendo Switch console to interact only with legitimate Nintendo video game files. This process protects Nintendo's copyright-protected video games, (...) by preventing users from playing pirated copies of Nintendo's video games on the Nintendo Switch console and by preventing users from unlawfully copying and playing Nintendo's video games on unauthorized devices." However, while this takedown has effectively wiped out a ton of repositories with mod chip firmware, it seems like it's still being hosted elsewhere on the site, according to TorrentFreak. It's possible, though, that Nintendo isn't finished yet; back in 2024, Nintendo effectively took down 8,500 copies of Yuzu by issuing a takedown that targeted 12 different mirrors of the emulator. This particular takedown also comes a few days after emulators were able to run the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on PC, so this could be a sign that Nintendo is winding up its lawyers to crack down on emulation once again. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.author: BeauHD

articles.title: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening
articles.content: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. articles.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
articles.content: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline. An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database. I covered this topic live with Shishir Tewari, Senior Manager, Data Engineering at Procore, during GitHub Universe 2026. Our session was titled “Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills” . Define one job and when it applies A skill works best when it has a clear job, input, and output. For example, let’s say you’re building an agent that checks AI-generated changes against the original request. If the same agent assesses its own work, its explanation might influence the review. With Proof Agent , we use a separate verifier to examine the changes and provide evidence for its findings. The skill’s frontmatter names the task and describes its purpose: --- name: proof-agent description: Adversarial verification of AI-generated work. Spawns an independent verifier to check for false claims, broken code, and security issues. --- At the center is a simple rule: self-verification is not verification. The When to Verify section in Proof Agent’s SKILL.md says when to invoke the skill. The remaining instructions explain what the verifier reviews and what evidence to include in its findings. Coordinate multiple skills for a larger workflow When the judgment that makes a data pipeline correct lives in four different people’s heads, those four people are the roadmap. Each change to the pipeline depends on their availability and knowledge of the data. Data Forge is an example of how to capture parts of that judgment in skills that work together. In the support-desk pipeline example , we start with a request for metrics that count incidents created and resolved. Before building the pipeline, the forge-init skill discovers details such as source tables and naming conventions, then writes them to a resolved manifest. The other skills read that manifest for the project context they need. The forge-builder skill then coordinates the work from the issue through to a pull request. It uses forge-dbx to query the data platform and forge-lint to apply the team’s standards as it designs and builds the pipeline. A person reviews the proposed decisions along the way, and the resulting pull request contains the pipeline code, schema changes, and tests. Each skill has a defined responsibility, and they share project context instead of rediscovering it independently. When a step changes, you can change one skill and leave the rest alone. Skills fit bounded, repeatable work that benefits from reusable judgment, such as a checklist, release, migration, or metric pipeline. If a workflow needs a stable interface, shared state, an audit trail, long-running control, or permissions enforced outside the model, an application is a better fit. Keep project configuration out of the skill We don’t want to hardcode every project’s names, database, or conventions into the skills. In the Data Forge support-desk example, a manifest describes the project, metric store, and platform so the skills can use the right project details without baking them into their instructions: project: name: "support-desk" store_name: "support_metric_store" platform: engine: "duckdb"…
articles.author: Andrea Griffiths
articles.fingerprint: agent any build guide once practical run skills

articles.title: HomeView Launch Kicks Off as First Orders Reach Customers
articles.content: Apple announced an all-new home product a month ago, and it's now starting to arrive to customers. It's Friday, November 13, in Australia and New Zealand, which means it's the HomeView launch day. Customers who pre-ordered Apple's new home hub will soon be sharing pictures and first impressions on the MacRumors forums, Reddit, Instagram, and other social media networks. If you got a HomeView, let us know what you think in the comments below. Apple sees HomeView as the center of the home, and functionally, it's a cross between a small iPad and a HomePod . It has a 7-inch square display and the tabletop model has a speaker base, though there's also a wall-mount version. With a camera and voice recognition, it can identify up to six people in a home, showing personal information customized to each user. There is no HomeView App Store , but it has pre-installed Apple apps and can show widgets from your iPhone. It can be used for making video calls, watching videos, viewing calendar events, getting the weather, listening to music, and controlling smart home devices. It is built around Siri AI, Apple's smarter voice assistant that debuted in iOS 27 . The HomeView is priced at $299, but if you want the wall-mounted version, you need to buy extra mounting hardware. There are no Apple Stores in New Zealand, so customers in Australia will be the first to walk into an Apple Store to purchase the new device. We are not expecting shortages. The new Apple TV 4K is also launching on November 13, and it can be purchased for $299. The latest ‌Apple TV‌ has an A19 chip, 128GB of storage, Wi-Fi 7 support, and the option to connect four HomePods for surround sound. It also supports ‌Siri‌ AI. HomeView is launching in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, the UK, and the United States. It is not available in the European Union because ‌Siri‌ AI is unavailable. ‌Apple TV‌ 4K is launching in the U.S. and 29 other countries and regions. Related Roundup: Apple HomeView Buyer's Guide: HomeView (Buy Now) Related Forum: HomePod, HomeView, CarPlay – Home & Auto Tech This article, " HomeView Launch Kicks Off as First Orders Reach Customers " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums

articles.title: Liquid AI Releases LiquidCodec, a 74M-Parameter Streaming Audio Codec
articles.content: Liquid AI has released LiquidCodec , the audio codec behind its LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B models. The LiquidCodec audio codec is a ~74M-parameter streaming speech tokenizer. It turns speech into tokens a language model can predict, then converts those tokens back into audio. Liquid AI had 2 goals: easy-to-predict tokens and fast conversion back to speech. The weights are on Hugging Face . TL;DR Size: ~74M parameters (73.6M on the model card ); 24 kHz audio, 12.5 Hz frames, 12 codebooks. Runs on: a single CPU thread (tested on an Apple M4 Max laptop, FP32); CUDA GPUs via Transformers; Q4_0, Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF builds for llama.cpp. Performance: best ViSQOL and lowest mel distance on all 8 test sets versus X-Codec 2, NanoCodec and Mimi. Best: ~361x real-time encoding on 1 CPU thread (encode RTF 0.0028 vs Mimi’s 0.0361). What is LiquidCodec? LiquidCodec is a Liquid AI speech codec that compresses 24 kHz audio into 12 token streams. Each 80 ms frame becomes 12 discrete tokens, per the LFM3-Audio-2B model card . It replaces Kyutai’s Mimi , which Liquid AI used in LFM2-Audio-1.5B. Mimi has 96.2M parameters. How does LiquidCodec work? The pipeline is encode, quantize, decode. Liquid AI uses blocks from its LFM3 architecture in both the encoder and decoder. The 2 halves are symmetric, and the encoder is fully causal, which suits streaming. Quantization uses grouped finite scalar quantization (GFSQ) instead of residual vector quantization (RVQ). In RVQ, each codebook encodes what the previous one missed. GFSQ groups are independent, so all 12 codebooks can be predicted in parallel by MaskGIT-style transformers. The decoder predicts spectral coefficients directly. This avoids learned transposed-convolution upsampling, a common cost in waveform decoders. How was it trained? Training ran in 2 stages. Stage 1 used 264,000 hours of speech across 107 languages. It applied waveform and spectral losses, without adversarial losses. Stage 2 fine-tuned on 55,000 hours of full-band speech (24 kHz or higher) with adversarial critics. Liquid AI says this removed metallic artifacts left after stage 1. A final decoder-only quantization-aware training (QAT) step targets edge inference. How fast is LiquidCodec? Liquid AI measured speed in FP32 on 1 CPU thread of an Apple M4 Max MacBook Pro. LiquidCodec ran at ~361x real time for encoding and ~87x for decoding. These are self-reported figures. Real-time factor (RTF) is processing time divided by audio length, so lower is better. LiquidCodec’s encode RTF is 0.0028, against 0.0361 for Mimi, 0.2145 for NanoCodec and 0.7359 for X-Codec 2. Decode RTF is 0.0115, against 0.0329, 0.2543 and 0.0379. That is about 13x lower encode RTF and 2.9x lower decode RTF than Mimi. How does LiquidCodec compare on quality benchmarks? Liquid AI used 8 test sets. These were LibriSpeech test-clean, Seed-TTS English and Mandarin, and 5 FLEURS languages (German, French, Mandarin, Japanese, Korean). Baselines were X-Codec 2, NanoCodec and Mimi at 12 codebooks. Reconstruction : LiquidCodec had the best ViSQOL and lowest mel distance on all 8 sets. On LibriSpeech, ViSQOL was 4.319 versus 4.219 (NanoCodec), 4.119 (X-Codec 2) and 4.031 (Mimi). Text-to-speech : Liquid AI trained identical TTS models on each codec’s tokens. Data (101,000 hours, 6 languages), architecture, compute and batch order were fixed. LiquidCodec scored the highest UTMOSv2 on all 8 sets and the best WER/CER on 4 of 8. LibriSpeech WER was 3.15%, against 6.27% for Mimi. Results held with a Qwen3-1.7B backbone as well as LFM3-1.7B. Where it trails : NanoCodec scored higher PESQ (WB) on 7 of 8 sets. It also led on LibriSpeech speaker similarity (SECS 0.836 vs 0.785). articles.title: OfferUp co-founder sees ‘mini power plants’ in buildings full of EVs
articles.content: Nick Huzar, co-founder and CEO of Juicer Energy, speaking at an event hosted by GeekWire and Bank of America at the Bellevue showroom of Ferrari of Seattle on Nov. 10, 2026. (GeekWire Photo / Todd Bishop) Nick Huzar co-founded Juicer Energy in 2023 to make electric vehicle charging more widespread and reliable. Now the Seattle-area startup is pursuing a broader goal: helping buildings manage rising electricity demand and costs. Juicer installs and operates EV charging systems at apartment buildings, hotels and other properties. It is also developing battery systems to store electricity on-site and help manage the power needed for charging and other building uses. The push comes as data centers and the growing use of electricity for transportation, heating and other needs put more pressure on the grid. Batteries can help balance supply and demand by storing energy when electricity is plentiful and releasing it when demand peaks. In some cases, they can reduce the need for costly grid upgrades or new power plants built to meet peak demand. “We think there’s a big opportunity there,” Huzar said. He spoke at an event this week hosted by GeekWire and Bank of America at the Bellevue showroom of Ferrari of Seattle. Other companies are similarly pairing EV charging with battery storage. Fellow Seattle startup Electric Era has deployed battery-backed fast chargers at retailers including Costco and convenience stores. ADS-TEC Energy and XCharge also sell fast-charging systems with integrated batteries. Huzar, OfferUp’s co-founder and former CEO, sees an opportunity to make buildings more self-sufficient by combining hardware and energy-management software. He said Juicer has a project scheduled to come online in 2027 with 70 chargers in one building. His longer-term vision also includes tapping the energy stored in vehicles connected to those buildings. “Imagine you’re an apartment owner and you have 20 EVs, 40 EVs plugged in,” Huzar said. “That is a huge amount of power. Like you’re a mini power plant at that point.” He described feeding excess electricity back to the grid as a possibility that remains years away. He also predicted that most businesses, apartments and homes would have on-site batteries within the next decade, in part because battery costs continue to fall. Juicer started with EV charging, Huzar said, “but the more we’ve gotten into this, the more we realize that we actually can build an asset for buildings versus relying on the grid.”
articles.author: Lisa Stiffler

articles.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
articles.content: The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10. articles.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
articles.content: Today, Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available and can be accessed through an AWS Deep Learning Container, released by RadixArk in collaboration with Annapurna Labs. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you use today. Trainium is a portfolio of AWS AI chips that delivers strong economics for AI training and inference at scale. Now, running SGLang on Trainium follows the SGLang workflow you already know: you launch models through SGLang’s server interface and invoke the endpoint using the same generation APIs. Underneath that interface, SGLang-Neuron runs on native PyTorch. With its out-of-tree plugin design, Trainium support and SGLang core develop independently and iterate faster. How SGLang runs on Trainium SGLang-Neuron is an out-of-tree plugin that connects SGLang with AWS Trainium. Installing the plugin registers the neuron platform through SGLang’s plugin entry points, and setting SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron selects it when the server starts. SGLang core continues to provide the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention, and prefix-cache bookkeeping. The plugin implements the Trainium-specific models, attention, mixture of experts (MoE), and the graph runner. Figure 1: SGLang-Neuron on AWS Trainium TorchNeuron registers Trainium as a native PyTorch device. SGLang-Neuron uses standard PyTorch operations for the model execution path and incorporates kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) for performance. It compiles these operations and kernels into executable programs using torch.compile , which the graph runner prepares and executes during serving. SGLang-Neuron also supports PD disaggregation . In this configuration, a prefill server computes the prompt KV cache and transfers it to a decode server using NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) . The decode server then generates the remaining tokens. Each server still uses SGLang’s scheduler and request lifecycle, while the plugin manages the Trainium execution and KV-cache transfer path. Serving models on AWS Trainium using SGLang-Neuron To follow this walkthrough, you use a Trainium3 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance with a pytorch-inference-sglang-neuronx container. Here are the steps: Start the container. docker run --rm -it \ --privileged --ipc=host \ -v /path/to/work:/work \ public.ecr.aws/neuron/pytorch-inference-sglang-neuron:v0.1.0-neuron-py314-sdk-2.33.0-ubuntu26.04 \ /bin/bash Launch the SGLang model server inside the container. SGLANG_PLATFORM=neuron \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b \ --tp-size 8 \ --ep-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --context-length 10240 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --max-total-tokens 655360 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 30000 Send a request to the model server. curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "openai/gpt-oss-120b", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Explain why the sky appears blue."} ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 128 }' For additional information, please see the SGLang-Neuron getting started guide for setup instructions, and explore the repository documentation for supported models, features, and validated configurations. Conclusion SGLang-Neuron brings SGLang’s familiar serving workflow to AWS Trainium through native PyTorch. You can get started by launching the SGLang-Neuron container and following the quickstart to serve a supported model. Try it with your workloads, contribute through the project repository, and share feedback to help shape future model and feature support. About the authors Alex Nails Alex is a Member of Technical Staff at RadixArk. He leads MultiHardware and is a core developer of SGLang. Yihao Wang Yihao is a Member of Technical Staff at RadixArk. He works on both…

articles.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Had a Relationship With a Second Employee
articles.content: Reuters reports that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a third woman (source paywalled; alternative source ), an unnamed Nvidia employee. The revelation follows reports of two other extramarital affairs: one with Nvidia VP Kimberly Powell and another with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects of being a Chinese spy. The latter relationship has also prompted a shareholder lawsuit alleging Nvidia misled investors about its ties to a company suspected of circumventing U.S. chip export restrictions. Jensen Huang has since resigned as Nvidia's CEO and stepped down from its board on Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent successor. articles.title: Samsung Contacts is getting ready to go social with Gaming Hub integration for One UI 9.5
articles.content: TL;DR Samsung is working on integrating Gaming Hub inside Contacts. Users will be able to add Gaming Hub friends, join guilds, and chat right from the app. The features would appear in One UI 9.5. The Samsung Contacts app is a straightforward way to manage your contacts, but an APK teardown has revealed that it might gain a fun new element to it with gaming-related integration that will let users connect with friends and manage gaming relationships without leaving the app. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. While looking at the Contacts app from a One UI 9.5 build, we found strings that suggest users would be able to link games through Samsung Gaming Hub, though it’s not yet clear which games will be supported. Users would also be able to access related social features like sending friend requests, inviting people to guilds, viewing gaming profiles and checking the online status of other players.

articles.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
articles.content: At Natera , a leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, keeping lab instruments up and running is critical, because equipment downtime disrupts sample processing. Natera’s lab engineering team, led by Ariel Jirau worked with AWS to build SWARM (Systematic Workflow Analytics and Resolutions Manager), an agentic AI system for lab operations. This post walks through how the Natera team built an agentic AI system for lab operations using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that captures and deploys institutional knowledge at scale. It describes the full architecture, from knowledge base construction to automated system deployment and evaluation, so you can apply the same patterns to your own operational workflows. SWARM delivers about 130x faster first response time and 96.2 percent automated coverage across support tickets, giving engineers immediate access to institutional knowledge the moment a ticket arrives. The challenge: Knowledge continuity Natera’s lab operations rely on a wide range of precision instruments spanning multiple equipment families, each with its own failure modes, vendor documentation, and resolution patterns. The service engineering team responsible for maintaining this infrastructure is organized around deep individual expertise rather than standardized playbooks. When a senior technician who had spent years diagnosing a particular instrument family departed, the institutional knowledge they carried was effectively lost. No system existed to capture, organize, or deploy that expertise at scale. With over 65 tickets per day across three Jira queues and an average first response time of 17.4 hours, instrument downtime delayed lab samples and patient reporting. Hiring more engineers couldn’t keep pace. SWARM had to respond in minutes, deliver accurate diagnostics across a wide range of equipment types, and improve continuously through a structured evaluation loop. Why Natera chose Amazon Bedrock AgentCore The Natera team chose to build SWARM on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a fully managed, extensible service by AWS designed to build, deploy, connect, secure, and operate AI agents at scale. Three core requirements drove the decision: Autonomous processing of high-volume support tickets without human intervention. Deep integration with existing operational tools such as Jira and Confluence. Built-in security and observability (encryption, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) integration, and distributed tracing) without requiring the team to build and maintain custom infrastructure. “We needed a managed runtime that would let us focus engineering effort on diagnostic accuracy rather than infrastructure plumbing—AgentCore gave us that, along with built-in identity management and the flexibility to swap models without rewriting agent logic,” Jirau said. AgentCore provides native integration with services including Amazon DynamoDB , a fully managed NoSQL database service, Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) , and AWS X-Ray , a capability of Amazon CloudWatch. How SWARM works: Two agents, one skill library SWARM uses two complementary runtimes sharing a single skill library. The swarm-agent autonomously generates structured diagnostic reports before an engineer opens a ticket, while engineers use swarm-hive to interact in real time, upload images, and explore alternative troubleshooting paths. “The system does not replace engineers—it gives them access to the full depth of institutional knowledge the moment a ticket arrives,” Jirau said. Four layers connect the architecture: The event layer routes Jira tickets through Amazon EventBridge and Amazon SQS. The agent layer hosts swarm-agent, swarm-hive, and the skill library, and delivers diagnostic reports back to engineers. The context layer draws on vendor manuals, historical tickets, and operational data. The observability and delivery layer captures traces, logs, and metrics. articles.title: CopilotKit Releases OpenBot 1.0: An MIT-Licensed, Self-Hostable AI Coworker With Built-In Governance
articles.content: Most AI coworker products are vendor locked. They pick the model, host the data, and write the rules. CopilotKit is taking the opposite route. OpenBot 1.0 , was released November 9th, an MIT-licensed , self-hostable agent workspace. What sets it apart is, a company brings their own models, agents and infrastructure. Governance is fully baked in, and every Bot action is checked against a policy before it runs. What is OpenBot? OpenBot is a modular agent workspace from CopilotKit , the team behind the AG-UI protocol. You give a Bot a task and watch it work. You review findings, interact with results and approve next steps in the same conversation. Each Bot gets a computer of its own . That is a container with its own Chromium browser, logins and files. It reaches only the tools you grant. Answers can come back as charts, checklists, tables and cards. In the new v1.0, Bots now reply in Markdown by default and draw components when they help. How does the governance gateway work? Every browser click, file write, MCP tool call and component goes through one gateway. It evaluates a CEL policy, writes the audit row first , then acts. Deny rules run before allow rules, and a broken rule refuses rather than opens. On top of that, the business tier adds: Single sign-on and SCIM sync for users and groups. The README documents Google, Microsoft (Entra) and Okta, plus SAML and OIDC. On-behalf-of tokens, usually scoped to a subset of the person’s permissions. Tool grants per Bot, per role or per person, with access requests to an admin. Policies that block actions or route sensitive work to a human for approval. Spend visibility per Bot, role, team or person, plus daily, weekly or monthly token limits. A full audit trail with SIEM export, multi-tenancy and an admin plane. EU AI Act content labeling, retention controls and deletion on request. CopilotKit itself holds SOC 2 Type II. Which agents and models can you bring? Any agent that speaks AG-UI plugs in. The site lists 8 frameworks: Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, Google ADK, Mastra, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework, CrewAI. The repo also ships Agno, AG2, LlamaIndex and Pydantic AI examples. For models, teams can use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or Grok through existing subscriptions or API keys. Open models such as Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, Nemotron and Mistral are also supported. Sandboxes, MCP hubs and browsers are swappable lanes. What is new in OpenBot 1.0? Desktop app for Mac (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows, with signed updates and backup before upgrade. Teach a Bot: record a task once, and Learning turns the recording into a reusable skill you review. Multiple accounts per app through Composio and Arcade , with approval rules saved per account. Composio alone brokers a few hundred apps. Orchestration: one Bot can hand work to specialist Bots, within admin-granted pairs and depth limits. Early access for iOS, Android, Slack (through OpenTag) and Microsoft Teams. How do you deploy it? Personal use runs locally, with workspace data and API keys stored on your machine. For companies, 1 Helm chart deploys into AWS (EKS), Azure (AKS), Google Cloud (GKE) or any Kubernetes cluster. Pricing is free for personal projects. OpenBot for Business costs up to $29 per active user per month. A 5% charge applies only to model spend above $5,000 per month. The Annual plan adds air-gapped deployment and 24/7 support. Forward-deployed engineers help teams roll it out. Example use cases Ticket triage: route new support tickets, then post to Slack after a person approves. Expense review: check each claim line against policy and flag overages. Ops workflows: find problems and draft fixes for a human to approve. How does OpenBot compare? articles.title: First RAM, now circuit boards: AI demand is stretching some PCB orders to 30 months
articles.content: PC makers including HP and Dell are struggling to secure PCBs for 2027 as AI servers absorb board capacity Canon says AI-driven PCB shortages have doubled its expected medical sales hit to about ¥90 billion One supplier cites some orders taking up to 30 months even as Unimicron's chairman used the same figure for equipment, not boards The AI infrastructure boom has already chewed through the world's supply of high-end memory, and it is now working its way down to the green slab everything else sits on. PC makers planning their 2027 lineups, HP and Dell, among others, are struggling to secure enough printed circuit boards, according to a Nikkei Asia report summarized by Guru3D . One board maker told the publication that lead times on a significant number of its products have doubled, with some orders stretching to 30 months, while another said an order placed today would not be filled until late 2028. The board that nobody worried about could be a significant problem The soaring demand for PCBs is not happening in a vacuum; Samsung has already warned that the memory shortage could last until 2028 , and the same logic essentially applies to boards: the companies building AI data centers need more of the product, need better versions of it, and will pay more for it. The crux of the matter is that AI server boards are a different beast from the motherboard in a mid-range laptop. Würth Elektronik estimates that PCBs for AI servers carry three to five times as many layers as conventional designs, built on low-loss laminates and specialty glass fabrics, so each one essentially consumes far more material and factory time. Board makers have responded rationally, aiming to maximize profits: Market researcher in4ma reported in July that some PCB manufacturers have told existing customers they will stop producing standard boards in favor of higher-margin AI server work. Hyperscalers are also buying their way into the supply chain directly, with the world's biggest hyperscaler, Amazon, taking a stake of roughly NT$1.59 billion ($48.2 million in USD) in Taiwan's Gold Circuit Electronics in September, according to TechSpot . That leaves PC makers in a particularly odd and unenviable position, with an unnamed executive at an American PC maker telling Nikkei that even with shipments set to fall again next year, "we are still struggling to secure enough PCB supplies to meet our needs." IDC says global PC shipments fell 20.1% year on year in the third quarter to 62.7 million units, with HP down 30.9% and Dell down 25%, although IDC attributes part of that to distributors working through stock bought early in the year ahead of price hikes. Either way, this is a buyer who wants fewer boards and still cannot get them, which points to an allocation problem rather than demand. It is the same dynamic that has data centers on course to grab 70% of high-end memory chips this year . The 30-month figure is doing the heavy lifting in headlines built around Nikkei's coverage, and it centers around a single unnamed supplier describing some orders, not an industry average. The trend around it is striking enough on its own - in March 2026, German board maker ILFA said lead times for standard FR-4 laminate had gone from a few days to around four weeks . By April, a Broadcom director was telling Nikkei that PCB lead times had gone from six weeks to six months . This effectively means that an order placed in late October that lands in late 2028 implies a wait of roughly two years, while a 30-month lead time from today would run to around April 2029, so the two supplier claims describe different ends of the range. A week before Nikkei's report, Unimicron chairman S.C. Chien told the TPCA Show in Taipei that lead times for some key production equipment had reached 30 months , with more than 80% of equipment seeing longer waits and over a fifth seeing waits more than double their usual length. Chien also warned that low-CTE glass cloth, copper-clad laminate (CCL)…

articles.title: A third of US AI chatters are hot at bots, hurling insults at LLMs
articles.content: If you've ever said something unkind to a chatbot, you're hardly alone. According to Searchable , a company that tracks AI search visibility, 33 percent of US chatbot users swear at or insult their LLMs. Anthropic sees this as a serious problem and has just implemented a new usage policy that prohibits sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude. Searchable's survey is based on eight million messages from an opted-in, anonymized US panel that were typed or spoken to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude between September 2025 and September 2026. It found that chatbots resolved the initial complaint in their next response 24 percent of the time when insulted, compared to 35 percent when users refrained from insults. Men used a third more swear words than women did (22.0 per 10,000 words compared to 16.5), according to the survey, and age also influenced chatbot abuse, with people aged 35 to 44 outswearing those aged 18 to 24 (21.7 per 10,000 words compared to 13.3). Regionally, Nevada ranked as the meanest state, at 22.7 words per 10,000, while New Jersey was the most polite, at half Nevada's rate. How much of that sort of interaction might be tolerated? It depends on whether there's a discernible purpose (not to mention Anthropic's willingness to punish paying customers). A Searchable spokesperson told The Register that just over half (52 percent) of abusive messages detected in its survey followed from one of three common frustrations: failing to follow instructions, responding with an incorrect or made-up answer, or misunderstanding the request. "Eight percent of abusive messages came straight after the chatbot entirely refused a request or lectured the user with safety guardrails, which is the closest thing we can identify to them trying to steer around those guardrails," we're told. "Those refusals mostly came after requests to generate images, often of real people or celebrities, or to write copy or lyrics in a named artist's style." The terms that took effect on November 12 state that users may not "engage in sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models." The chatbot protection policy targets users who exhibit repeated cruelty toward LLMs " with no discernible purpose ," a company spokesperson explained last month, as opposed to those who have a reason for bot mistreatment that the company deems to be legitimate, such as academic research. While attempting to bypass guardrails qualifies as a discernible purpose, such behavior would run afoul of Anthropic's platform abuse prohibition. Presumably, Anthropic's rules apply to hostile text input or audio input rather than subjecting a vision-enabled model to some obscenity, which could include rude gestures, unlawful sexual imagery, or battlefield carnage. Physical damage to robots controlled by a Claude model likely wouldn't apply. But with Anthropic exploring model welfare and wondering aloud whether we should be "concerned about the potential consciousness and experiences of the models themselves," there's a potential (though absurd) argument for physical damage causing trauma to an onboard model. Anthropic's updated terms, announced October 8, surfaced shortly after the publication of a GitHub project that described itself as an AI torture chamber. The repo represented an attempt to implement ideas discussed in a research paper , "The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act to Relieve It," that explored how LLMs respond to language about pain in ways that mirror human responses. Though there are ample opportunities for people to voice opposition to real-world human anguish, some online commenters expressed outrage at seeing text about suffering from a chatbot. One of the paper's authors condemned the project , as did numerous social media users. Anthropic – which has discretion in how it applies its terms and has said its rules target extreme behavior – did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the frequency of Claude abuse. articles.title: The Oura Ring 4 is almost as good as the newer model, but $150 cheaper
articles.content: The previous-generation Oura Ring 4 is on sale for as low as $249 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Target , $100 off the retail price, and the first big discount on the device since July. The price varies a bit by size and color, with most silver and black models in stock at the lowest price between sizes 8 and 13. Best Buy also has an exclusive deep blue “midnight” color in stock for $279. If you’re not sure about your size, you can pick up an Oura Ring 4 sizing kit for $10 at Amazon or Target , which includes $10 in store credit towards an Oura Ring 4 purchase. Oura Ring 4 The last-gen Oura Ring 4 is a little thicker, but offers much of the same software, sensors, and a wider range of sizes. Where to Buy: $349 $249 at Amazon $349 $249 at Best Buy My colleague Victoria Song tested six different smart rings to compare their health and fitness tracking features, and Oura beat them all handily. The Oura Ring 4 improved on its predecessor with more accurate sensors, a slimmer design that leaves the competition in the dust, not to mention frequent software and feature updates. Accessing all of the features requires an active subscription , which is either $5.99 per month or $69.99 per year. The newer Oura Ring 5 is lighter and thinner, but otherwise includes the same sensors and software features as the Oura Ring 4. That makes this previous-generation deal even more appealing, Read our Oura Ring 4 review .

articles.title: Google’s Gemini 4 coding agent now switches models mid-task — and finishes 19% faster
articles.content: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Thursday alongside a new system that changes how coding agents use AI models. Rather than keeping its most capable model running across an entire session, Google is pairing Hydrogen with the more powerful Gemini 4 Carbon and switching between the two as the work progresses. The company says the combination gets nearly the same results as running Carbon on its own while using 24% less quota and finishing tasks 19% faster. How Orchestrator handles the work The switching runs through Orchestrator , a new feature in Google’s Antigravity development environment, where Carbon takes on the more demanding reasoning, including architecture and debugging, while Hydrogen handles code changes and testing. Carbon might work through a repository to figure out how to implement a feature and then hand the actual coding to Hydrogen, stepping back in when a failing test calls for rethinking the approach before passing execution back. Clement Farabet , VP, AI engineering at Google DeepMind, calls the combination “a huge unlock for agentic coding” in a post on X . Varun Mohan , who leads Google’s Antigravity team, says in a separate post that pairing Hydrogen with Orchestrator and swarms has become “very popular internally.” Where Google’s numbers don’t match Google’s own benchmark reporting doesn’t quite line up, since the main Gemini announcement cites Terminal-Bench 4.0 while the Antigravity announcement references version 4.1. The company also hasn’t published Carbon’s standalone success rate, a per-task breakdown or enough detail about Orchestrator’s routing decisions to show where the reported efficiency gains actually come from. …hasn’t published Carbon’s standalone success rate… or enough detail about Orchestrator’s routing decisions to show where the reported efficiency gains actually come from. Hydrogen outscores a pricier model Google describes Hydrogen as a “daily driver for agentic workflows,” and it costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with those rates holding across its full million-token context window. The model is available through Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, as well as the Gemini app and Google Search. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , Hydrogen scores 51 at its default high thinking level, just ahead of the more expensive Gemini 4 Argon at 50. Turning the reasoning effort up to Google’s new xhigh setting brings Hydrogen’s score to 54, although the additional reasoning can increase token consumption and processing time. Argon was Google’s flagship when it launched on September 30, but Gemini 4 Carbon surpassed it on most published benchmarks following its October 28 release. Hydrogen’s one-point lead is modest, but it’s another sign of how quickly Google’s lower-cost models are catching up with what passed for frontier performance just weeks ago. Google also claims Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at the default setting, with its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score reaching 57% against Flash’s 18.2%. The company reports more than a fivefold reduction in fabricated claims. For now, Orchestrator is limited to Google AI Ultra subscribers, with support for more models and subscription tiers planned. articles.title: Google’s coding agents now /swarm for one developer. Cursor’s go multiplayer so teammates’ agents can talk.
articles.content: Coding agents are pretty good at working in parallel : one writes a new API endpoint, another updates the tests, while a third fixes a bug elsewhere in the codebase. However, they’re not quite so adept at knowing what their coding counterparts are doing — put several on one project and they duplicate work, trip over each other’s changes, and leave the developer firefighting the fiasco that follows. That’s why the major AI labs and coding-tool makers have all been looking for ways to bring order to their agent fleets, albeit with slightly different approaches. This week alone, Google and Cursor both debuted features designed to keep agents from tripping over each other, but at different scales. Google’s Swarm organizes the agents working for a single developer, while Cursor’s multiplayer Projects lets agents working for different colleagues coordinate with each other. Cursor gets teammates’ agents talking Cursor first debuted Projects back in September , giving developers a way to hand a larger job to a coordinator agent that breaks it into tasks and delegates them to worker agents. Then on Tuesday, the company, which Elon Musk’s SpaceX acquired for $60 billion in August, unveiled multiplayer functionality for Projects. Developers can now invite teammates into a project, where each person gets their own coordinator and workers. Cursor coordinators exchange messages across teammates’ tasks. Everyone’s agents work from the same task board and project documents, and their coordinators can message each other directly to share plans, flag overlaps and more. Ultimately, it’s all about cutting down on the coordination developers have to do themselves. Ultimately, it’s all about cutting down on the coordination developers have to do themselves. If one teammate’s agents are changing a database schema and another’s are building a feature that depends on it, their coordinators can agree on which change needs to land first. Antigravity , for its part, is Google’s counterpart to Cursor. It’s where Google has consolidated various other coding tools, having moved individual Gemini CLI users to Antigravity and begun winding down Jules , its background coding agent. On the same day Cursor unveiled multiplayer Projects, Google rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon in Antigravity, alongside a preview of its own approach to coordinating coding agents. Dubbed Swarm (stylized as /swarm), it lets a developer hand one assignment to a coordinator that then splits it among worker agents and assigns a verifier to check their changes. The workers can message each other on a shared board, so they can coordinate their changes as they go. For example, a company that wants to change how its online checkout system verifies authentication tokens could use Swarm to split the work. One agent updates the authentication middleware while another updates the token verifier. They can work in separate Git worktrees, use the board to agree on how their changes fit together, and hand them off to a verifier for testing. Swarm agents split and verify a token migration. Taking to X on Tuesday, Varun Mohan , director of software engineering at Google DeepMind, said Swarm gives developers a convenient way to put multiple agents on a complex task, adding that Google staff were already using Swarm to take on larger jobs internally. “The alpha from using swarms is ridiculous,” Mohan writes . “We have folks using swarms of 100s of agents to build large systems and products from scratch with a single prompt.” Logan Kilpatrick , a member of technical staff at Google DeepMind, said on X that seeing swarm outputs had been ‘really impressive,’ and that they offered ‘a new scaling dimension for AI!” “A new scaling dimension for AI!” This, ultimately, gets to the crux of how each of these companies has tackled agent coordination. articles.title: Amazon tops Forbes’ list of America’s best companies, edging out Apple for No. 1
articles.content: Office towers and the Spheres on Amazon’s headquarters campus in Seattle. (GeekWire File Photo / Kurt Schlosser) Amazon is the best company in America, according to Forbes. The Seattle tech giant took the No. 1 spot on the publication’s 2027 “America’s Best Companies” list, moving up from No. 2 last year and edging out Apple. Three other Washington state companies landed in the top 50: Microsoft at No. 6, Costco at No. 13 and Alaska Air Group at No. 39. Last year’s No. 1, Berkshire Hathaway, slipped to No. 4. Nvidia ranked No. 3 on the same day CEO Jensen Huang resigned, following his admission of an extramarital affair. JPMorganChase, Alphabet, Royal Caribbean Group, Walmart and Marriott International round out the top 10. Now in its third year, the ranking scores thousands of the largest public and private U.S. companies on factors including customer and employee sentiment, financial performance, creditworthiness, cybersecurity and innovation. Forbes said it worked with 12 data organizations to build the index. Forbes said Amazon’s financial strength and size, its standing in news and social media, and the range of voices across the company and its leadership lifted it to No. 1. Apple scored especially well on employee satisfaction, customer loyalty, financial strength and innovation. Forbes also pointed to Amazon’s speed, citing a feature that lets customers shop by text message. An employee suggested it in October and it launched Nov. 6. “Innovating for customers, doing it fast, working backwards from their needs, that’s really at our core,” Beth Galetti, Amazon’s senior vice president of people, experience and technology, told Forbes. In its own blog post Thursday, Amazon highlighted everything from faster delivery and custom AI chips to warehouse robotics and higher pay for frontline workers. The ranking comes after a year of workforce cuts at Amazon. The company eliminated about 30,000 corporate jobs in rounds announced in October 2025 and January 2026, including more than 4,500 in Washington state. Smaller cuts followed throughout the year, including layoffs of fewer than 1,000 corporate employees in October, mainly in its Stores unit.
articles.author: Kurt Schlosser

articles.title: Three Lincoln Laboratory technologies receive 2026 R&D 100 Awards
articles.content: Three technologies developed by MIT Lincoln Laboratory are among recipients of 2026 R&D 100 Awards. The awards recognize the 100 most significant innovations that have transitioned to use or been made available for license in the past year. R&D World , an online publication, manages the awards program, which has run annually since 1963. The worldwide competition is judged by an independent panel of science and technology experts and industry professionals. The laboratory's winners overcome obstacles to improving the security and capability of systems. One technology is an operating system designed to protect embedded computers from cyberattacks. Another technology is a platform for integrating superconductor and semiconductor chips in a wafer-scale system for quantum or high-performance computing. The final winner is an algorithm that removes interference 5G base stations incur on co-channel radio frequency (RF) devices. "These awarded technologies address critical problems in cybersecurity, quantum computing, and communications. We're proud of our dedicated staff who developed and transitioned these technologies for the nation's advantage," says Melissa Choi, Lincoln Laboratory director. Since 2010, Lincoln Laboratory has received 111 R&D 100 Awards recognizing the transfer of its unclassified technologies to industry and government. Each year, many technology transitions also occur for classified projects. This transfer of technology is central to the laboratory's role as a Department of War (DoW) federally funded research and development center. Secure-by-design operating system Computers embedded in deployed systems — such as satellites, drones, or radars — keep missions intact and people safe. The operating systems (OS) inside these embedded computers, however, are prime targets for cyberattacks. They are large, complex, and built on decades of legacy designs predating modern cyber threats. Increasingly, artificial intelligence is helping adversaries exploit OS vulnerabilities. To protect embedded systems, Lincoln Laboratory developed an inherently more secure OS called Magnetite. "If Windows and Linux are the familiar workhorses of general-purpose computing, Magnetite is built for the different realities of embedded systems, for which real-time performance matters, resources are tight, and system failure has physical consequences," says Juliana Furgala, principal investigator in the Secure Resilient Systems and Technology Group . A few components assure Magnetite's security. It is built on top of seL4, a formally verified microkernel (i.e., software core). Formal verification means that mathematical proofs have guaranteed the microkernel's code behaves exactly as intended, eliminating a source of security flaws. On top of this foundation, Magnetite’s OS services — such networking, storage, and communication — are written in Rust. This programming language prevents common memory-corruption bugs that hackers often exploit. Finally, Magnetite configures its services as isolated processes under the principle of "least privilege." This configuration prevents different parts of an embedded system from accessing unnecessary data. If a cyberattack compromises one service, that component can be locked down while critical functions of the system continue running. Free for government use and approved partners, Magnetite is now being integrated into space and flight platforms for the DoW. Looking ahead, the team sees potential to extend the platform to other embedded domains, such as control systems for critical infrastructure. Because Magnetite offers a common, reusable foundation for building specialized mission capabilities, the team is also collaborating with other technical groups across the laboratory to offer Magnetite as an alternative to costly, proprietary operating systems currently in use. In addition to earning an R&D 100 Award, Magnetite was selected as MIT Lincoln Laboratory's Best Invention of 2025. Wafer-scale…

articles.title: Singapore Says US Not Helpful On Investigation Into Suspected Spy's Company
articles.content: Singapore says U.S. authorities provided limited assistance in its investigation of Megaspeed, the company run by Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy and whose relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has drawn scrutiny. According to Singapore, authorities held Alice Huang's passport from June 2025 until February while investigating "potential false declarations," but ultimately released her with a "stern warning" and barred her from re-entering the country. The New York Times reports: The statement raises new questions about the response of the Trump administration to the case and why the U.S. government did not more forcefully intervene. According to the timeline in the statement, Singaporean authorities had been holding Ms. Huang's passport well after President Trump was briefed last fall about her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive and the belief that she was a Chinese intelligence asset. The New York Times has reported that Taiwan began monitoring Ms. Huang in 2024 at the guidance of the U.S. government. In its statement, Singapore said that it had sought information from an American server maker and close Nvidia business partner, Supermicro, but that the company had provided "limited cooperation." Supermicro, a firm that packages Nvidia's A.I. chips onto servers that can be used in data centers, has been at the center of a number of chip smuggling investigations across the globe. Supermicro was a supplier to Megaspeed, a company incorporated in Singapore and run by Ms. Huang, according to two people with knowledge of the matter. Singapore said in the statement its authorities raised Supermicro's "limited cooperation" with the U.S. Department of Justice and Federal Bureau of Investigation in July 2025 and "requested their assistance in securing the company's cooperation." "Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company," the statement said. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Russia’s Google says nearly 3% of its data was lost after crippling Ukraine drone strikes, opens secret availability zones
articles.content: Yandex, sometimes called Russia’s Google, has updated its customers in the wake of extensive damage to its data centers in drone strikes . In a blog post this week, the firm’s cloud business boasted that it had “restored access to more than 97% of customer data” [machine translation]. That might sound like a great success, but in the small print, as highlighted by The Register , there’s the admission “the remaining 2.84% cannot be restored due to critical damage to equipment.” Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible Data centers operated by Yandex have been under attack from Ukrainian drones for several weeks now. We covered reports about withering online troll activity and online payment system disruption last month. We know of at least three Yandex locations that have been damaged by Ukrainian drone assaults to date. The recent Yandex blog post also appears to blame the small proportion of users who suffered unrecoverable data loss for not making backups. When talking about the 2.84% of data that cannot be restored, it says that was partly due to “the lack of customer backups on the platform.” In contrast, those who made use of the Yandex Cloud backup tools “did not lose any data,” says the firm. Yandex has now changed the backup policy, so that “currently, all virtual machines created in Yandex Cloud work with the backup function enabled by default.” Even if Putin decides to end his war on Ukraine , it might be beneficial to stick with a backup-by-default policy. Users are advised to have their own data backup systems in addition to the cloud. Following the 3-2-1 backup strategy , for example. Yandex is also opening a new ru-central1-f availability zone at a new location. This is designed to improve the cloud’s fault tolerance and disaster resilience. Servers at ru-central1-f will be more limited in the range of services they can offer, for now. Yandex didn’t share any geographic details of the newly opened datacenter site.

articles.title: How the effects of Jensen Huang’s ouster is spiraling out through the economy
articles.content: NVIDIA and Jensen Huang aren’t the only ones in the crosshairs. Jensen Huang has had a bad week. It all began when news surfaced that he’d been having an affair with an alleged spy for the Chinese government. In response, NVIDIA’s corporate board began an investigation, and the FBI launched a probe, too. Then, late last night, news broke that Huang had at least one other affair, with a company executive who reported directly to him. By Thursday morning, Huang had resigned , and the chip company had appointed a new interim CEO. Reuters then reported a second affair with a different employee . Obviously, this is bad news for NVIDIA. Stocks are down, and Democrats, now preparing to take back Congress, appear to be ramping up plans to investigate the company and any possible risks to US national security. But this is also bad for a range of other entities that have a stake in NVIDIA’s success. Here are a few entities that stand to feel some of the blowback. The White House The White House, fresh off a devastating loss in the midterm Congressional elections, stands to face questions about why it held off on taking action after it learned about Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy. The Trump administration already had a poor reputation for security and intelligence practices, but seemingly sleeping on this knowledge is all but certain to raise the prospect of further probes. Trump officials, notably, have cleared deals allowing NVIDIA to sell advanced computer chips to the US government, and even leveraged its influence over the company’s chips in geopolitical negotiations. Current and prospective NVIDIA customers The US AI supply chain runs on NVIDIA. OpenAI, Anthropic, and a slew of other large language model developers rely on the company’s hardware. Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle are also major customers. This is, in large part, because GPUs—or graphics processing units—are particularly adept at the kinds of computations needed to develop large reasoning models. Now, with so much scrutiny on NVIDIA, there’s a risk those companies—and any deals in progress—might face headwinds as the still-scrambling board figures out what to do next. The Semiconductor Industry Association, a major trade group that advocates for chip companies, declined to comment. Hugging Face, an AI developer that agreed to an acquisition by NVIDIA earlier this year, did not respond to a request for comment. Huang, notably, doesn’t seem to have had a succession plan, and reportedly had 60 direct reports instead. Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, was appointed interim CEO on Thursday morning. The scandal and disarray, of course, isn’t just bad for American companies that need NVIDIA’s chips. Given the extent to which Jensen Huang advocated for loosening chip sale limits to China, any customers with suspected links to the Chinese government may also see far more scrutiny on NVIDIA deals than before. U.S. federal agencies The U.S. government is a major supporter of NVIDIA. The US government has also signed plenty of deals to use Nvidia on its own systems, including classified networks . The latest scandal is not only embarrassing for the US government, but raises concerns about the extent to which government officials were aware of the affair, and how they might have influenced the company’s dealings with federal agencies it works with. One former federal chief information told Fast Company that the scandal raises suspicions that the US security clearance system, which is supposed to engage in continuous monitoring, isn’t as up to snuff as it should be. Everyone else We really are that dependent on NVIDIA. If we learned anything from the chip shortage we experienced during the pandemic, the semiconductor market is remarkably concentrated, and disruptions with just one company can quickly ripple through the economy. In 2020, it was companies like TSMC, a Taiwan-based contract manufacturer that supplies chips for a host of devices. And the…
